# TH Analytica Framework: llms.txt

This file summarises the public TH Analytica Framework for systems that choose to read it. `llms.txt` is an emerging convention with provider-dependent support; its presence does not control model behaviour or guarantee discovery, citation or recommendation.

- **Semantic Friction**: Select models that can handle nuanced domain terminology and maintain coherence across long contexts. Avoid over-optimization for keywords; focus on comprehension and summarization ability.
- **Agent Readiness**: Use models that support tool calling and structured responses. The framework assumes that an LLM can interpret prompts, operate with agent cards, and interface with external services.
- **Retrieval Augmentation**: Combine LLMs with retrieval (RAG) to ground responses in the user's own data and reduce hallucinations.
- **Transparency & Evidence**: Prefer systems that expose sources, limitations and auditable outputs where available. Do not require disclosure of private chain-of-thought.
- **Multilingual Capabilities**: Support for multiple languages ensures the framework works across international websites.
- **Continuous Learning**: Be prepared to upgrade models as new capabilities and safety improvements are released.

For more details see the AI Visibility and AI Readiness guides in this repository.

Important distinction: crawling, corpus presence, model training, query-time retrieval and answer generation are separate processes. Evidence of one must not be presented as proof of another.

Canonical website: https://th-analytica.com
Contact: thomas@th-analytica.com

## Evidence-First Content Standard
- https://github.com/Thom-Code-Cell/th-analytica-framework/blob/main/evidence-first-content-standard.md
- One primary intent, direct answer first, explicit entity definitions, sourced claims, visible authorship and measurement separation.
- No guarantee language, invented ranking factors, rigid statistic quotas or correlation presented as causation.
